## What Is an EchoStar Internship?


An EchoStar internship is a paid, 10–12 week summer placement through the company's Build Your Future program that puts college students into real roles across Satellite Communications, Software Engineering, RF Engineering, Data Science, Cybersecurity, and Business Operations at a global telecommunications company generating[$15 billion in annual revenue with over 6,000 patents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EchoStar) . Following the January 2024 reunification of DISH Network under EchoStar, all internships are posted through the unified careers portal at jobs.echostar.com. Interns may work on products spanning DISH satellite TV, HughesNet satellite broadband (deployed across[9 million VSAT terminals in 100+ countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hughes_Network_Systems) ), Boost Mobile wireless, or Sling TV streaming. The company also runs a Pathfinder program for career exploration and a 2-year Management Training rotational for recent graduates. Interns rate the experience[4.0 out of 5 on Glassdoor from 6 reviews with 100% recommending](https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/DISH-Intern-Reviews-EI_IE4501.0,4_KO5,11.htm) , significantly above the broader employee rating.

### Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open


EchoStar's Build Your Future program runs a relatively small corporate intern class compared to the company's scale. Rolling review historically rewards early applicants, and the company's emphasis on satellite communications, 5G wireless, and streaming technology means they look for candidates who already show technical depth in RF engineering, software development, data analysis, or cybersecurity. The 2026 bankruptcy filings at Dish DBS and Hughes add uncertainty to internship availability, which makes early application even more important: if seats are offered, they will likely fill faster than in prior cycles. Do not wait until spring 2027 to check whether postings are live. By that point, any available positions may already be filled. Early application plus shown technical skills and genuine interest in EchoStar's product portfolio is the formula.

## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


EchoStar has not published a rigid list of eligibility criteria, but patterns from prior cycles and recruiter expectations point to the following:


• **Enrollment:** currently enrolled in an accredited undergraduate or graduate program as a rising sophomore, junior, senior, or graduate student.


• **GPA:** 3.0 preferred but not a strict requirement. EchoStar does not list a hard GPA threshold. Practical skills and relevant technical experience carry significant weight.


• **Work authorization:** US work authorization required. Some technical roles involving satellite systems or government contracts may require US citizenship or the ability to obtain security clearance (Hughes has government contracts for satellite services).


• **Additional:** valid driver's license may be required for field-facing roles. Drug testing and background check are part of the standard hiring process.


### Does EchoStar Have a Hard GPA Cutoff?


No published cutoff exists. EchoStar values practical technical capability over pure academic metrics. What matters more in practice is shown skill in satellite communications, RF engineering, software development, data analysis, or cybersecurity. The company's Pathfinder program emphasizes career growth through skills, not grades. If your GPA is below 3.0 but you have a finished technical project in a relevant domain, that evidence speaks louder than a number.

## What Is the EchoStar Application and Interview Process Like?


EchoStar publishes a five-stage hiring process on its careers page. Based on aggregated intern reports and the company's own published guidance, the timeline runs 4–8 weeks from application to offer:


1. **Apply at[jobs.echostar.com](https://www.echostar.com/careers)** with a tailored resume. Highlight satellite communications, RF engineering, software development, or data analysis coursework and projects. Use keywords from the specific posting.


2. **Initial screening** (week 1–2). A phone or video call with a recruiter covering your background, interest in EchoStar, and availability. The company states it extends its most competitive offer upfront, so salary negotiation is generally not expected.


3. **Behavioral interview using the STAR method** (weeks 2–4). EchoStar publishes its five core behavioral questions on its careers page, covering problem-solving, teamwork, feedback reception, adaptability, and customer focus. Prepare STAR-format answers for each.


4. **Culture-fit questionnaire or additional assessment** (weeks 3–5). An additional evaluation round that may include personality or values alignment questions.


5. **Offer and onboarding** (weeks 5–8). Background check and drug testing required. Some technical roles may require additional security clearance processing.


Because EchoStar publishes its own behavioral interview guide, candidates have a rare advantage: you know exactly what they will ask. Prepare specific STAR answers for all five questions and practice them out loud. Reference specific EchoStar products (HughesNet, DISH Hopper, Sling TV, Boost Mobile) to demonstrate genuine interest. Our[HireVue question guide with a free AI mock tool](https://www.extern.com/post/hirevue-interview-questions-2025-free-ai-mock-tool) covers the same behavioral-question pressure and format.

## How Do You Stand Out at a Company Navigating Restructuring?


Three moves, all executable before fall 2026. First, verify and apply early: check jobs.echostar.com now to see if positions are live, and apply in week one of any posting. Rolling review and a small corporate class mean the first applicants get the most seats, especially during a period of uncertainty. Second, show the cross-domain technical breadth that defines EchoStar's portfolio. The company spans satellite TV, satellite broadband, wireless, and streaming, so demonstrate that you can bridge multiple technology domains with project work in software development, data analysis, or cybersecurity. Third, prepare for EchoStar's published behavioral questions. The company uniquely publishes its five core STAR questions on its careers page. Arrive with polished answers that show adaptability and customer focus, two values the company screens for explicitly. And acknowledge the restructuring context: interviewers will respect candidates who understand the business situation and frame the internship as a learning opportunity regardless of organizational uncertainty.

## FAQ


### Can I still apply for a summer 2026 EchoStar internship?


No. The summer 2026 class started in May/June 2026 and those postings closed earlier in the year. The next open cycle is summer 2027. Based on prior-cycle patterns, EchoStar has historically posted summer internships between September and November, so check jobs.echostar.com now. Given the company's 2026 restructuring, verify whether positions are being offered before applying.


### How much do EchoStar interns get paid?


EchoStar interns earn approximately $20.79 per hour on average based on 7 salary reports on Indeed. Under the DISH brand, the average is $23.39 per hour, and engineering interns average $26.05. The highest-paying locations include Foster City, California at approximately $35.90 per hour. The company states it extends its most competitive offer upfront.


### Where are EchoStar internships located?


Most corporate and engineering internships are based at EchoStar's headquarters in Englewood, Colorado or the Hughes Network Systems campus in Germantown, Maryland. Additional positions have been posted in Littleton, Colorado, Marlborough, Massachusetts, and Foster City, California. EchoStar has not publicly confirmed a fully remote internship track.


### What departments offer EchoStar internships?


EchoStar hires interns across Software Engineering, Electrical and RF Engineering, Data Science, Cybersecurity, Network Engineering, Hardware Engineering, Product Management, Marketing, Finance, Sales, HR, and Legal. Interns may work on products spanning DISH TV, HughesNet, Boost Mobile, or Sling TV depending on team placement.


### Does EchoStar require a minimum GPA for internships?


A 3.0 GPA is typically preferred but not a strict requirement. EchoStar does not list a hard GPA threshold on its careers page. Practical skills, relevant project work, and shown technical competence in satellite communications, software development, or data analysis carry more weight than academic metrics at this company.


### What is the EchoStar internship interview process like?


EchoStar uses a five-stage process: online application, recruiter screen, behavioral interview using the STAR method, culture-fit assessment, and offer with background check. The company uniquely publishes its five core behavioral questions on its careers page, covering problem-solving, teamwork, feedback, adaptability, and customer focus.


### Does EchoStar sponsor visas for interns?


No public information confirms visa sponsorship for EchoStar interns. The company requires US work authorization. Some technical roles involving satellite systems or government contracts may require US citizenship or security clearance. International students with existing CPT or OPT authorization may be eligible for non-restricted roles.


### Is EchoStar still hiring interns given the bankruptcy filings?


EchoStar's Dish DBS subsidiary filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2026, and Hughes Network Systems filed separately in August 2026. The company continues to operate its consumer brands and core technology infrastructure. Whether summer 2027 internships will be offered depends on restructuring outcomes. Check jobs.echostar.com regularly for the latest hiring status.


EchoStar's technical portfolio remains genuinely impressive: 6,000-plus patents, satellite infrastructure spanning 100-plus countries, and brands across TV, broadband, wireless, and streaming. If positions are posted, the small corporate class fills fast on rolling review. Spend the runway building proof: a[remote Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships) turns "interested in satellite and telecom" into a finished project a fall 2026 application can point at.
